messages.author: d9ec245234a3bd75
messages.subject: Large LOD peaks
parts:
Hello,
I have a question and I hope it isn't too specific for an answer...
I performed scanone() for 93 individuals from an F2 cross family (Family 65 in the photo, trait is day to death since all individuals died in my experiment). I get many peaks with a very high LOD score, but none of them are above the LOD significance threshold after 1000 permutations. I did the same thing for 3 other families, but ran a 2-part model since my trait was day to death conditional on survival (Family 11, 43, and 22). There is much more distinct peaks for the 3 families with the 2-part model. My question is regarding the Family 65 LOD plot: have I coded something wrong along the way, or entered my data incorrectly? The peaks for 65 seem wonky and I can not figure out why. Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Large LOD peaks
parts:
In an F2, the curves should be more smooth. So yes, something is wrong.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Large LOD peaks
parts:
If you're estimating the genetic map and getting lengths > 1000 cM, that indicates a problem in the data. 
If you're getting a warning about that when you load the data, that suggests that you have marker positions in basepairs rather than cM. It would be best to at least convert to Mbp, as an approximation of basepairs.

But my guess, from the rapid fluctuation in the LOD score, is that nearby markers have radically different genotypes, but there are many possible underlying causes.

karl
